title: Formal objects are independent of a cofinal ideal filtration
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $k$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the category $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with specified residue field $k$ and local maps inducing the identity on $k$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be any category cofibred in groupoids on $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $C$ be a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra with residue field $k$, and let $I_1\supseteq I_2\supseteq\cdots$ be proper ideals cofinal with the powers of $\mathfrak m_C$: for every $r$ some $I_n\subseteq\mathfrak m_C^r$ and for every $n$ some $\mathfrak m_C^r\subseteq I_n$. The groupoid of compatible systems $u_n\in\mathcal F(C/I_n)$, with transition isomorphisms and compatible families of arrows, is equivalent to the groupoid of formal objects on $C$. If $u$ corresponds to $\xi$, then its value at $C\to C/I_n$ is compatibly isomorphic to $u_n$. More generally, for any local $R$-algebra map $C\to A$ inducing the identity on the specified residue field $k$ with $A\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$ factoring through $C/I_n$, the value $\xi_A$ is compatibly isomorphic to the transport of $u_n$ to $A$.

source.place: Tag 06H6 (lemma-formal-objects-different-filtration), including the evaluations supplied by its cofinal reindexing construction.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_C$, $B_n=C/I_n$ and $D_r=C/\mathfrak m^r$, with all indices positive. Every proper ideal of the local ring $C$ lies in $\mathfrak m$. For each $n$, cofinality supplies $N\ge1$ with $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq I_n\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The quotient lemma therefore makes $B_n$ Artinian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I_n$; likewise $D_r$ is Artinian local. The residue identification for both is $C/\mathfrak m=k$. All quotient maps below are local $R$-maps inducing the identity on $k$, so these rings and maps belong to the test category. Choose nondecreasing functions $p,q:\mathbf N_{>0}\to\mathbf N_{>0}$ with $p(r)\ge r$, $q(n)\ge n$, $I_{p(r)}\subseteq\mathfrak m^r$ and $\mathfrak m^{q(n)}\subseteq I_n$. Recursively take each new index at least its predecessor and its argument, and at least a cofinality witness; decreasing ideals and powers preserve the required containments. Repetitions are allowed.

source.place: Tag 06H6 (lemma-formal-objects-different-filtration), selection of indices; test-ring verification using algebra.tex Tag 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0).

proof.text: Use the coherent transport functors of the deformation-test definition. For an ideal inclusion $J\subseteq K$, denote transport along $C/J\to C/K$ by $T_{J,K}$. Its specified composition isomorphism identifies $T_{K,L}T_{J,K}$ with $T_{J,L}$; throughout, insert these isomorphisms. If $u$ is an $I$-system, let $\tau_{a,b}:T_{I_a,I_b}u_a\xrightarrow{\sim}u_b$ for $a\ge b$ be its iterated transition. Its compatibility reads $\tau_{a,c}=\tau_{b,c}\circ T_{I_b,I_c}(\tau_{a,b})$. Define $(Eu)_r=T_{I_{p(r)},\mathfrak m^r}u_{p(r)}$. For $s\ge r$, its transition to level $r$ is $T_{I_{p(r)},\mathfrak m^r}(\tau_{p(s),p(r)})$, after identifying its source with $T_{I_{p(s)},\mathfrak m^r}u_{p(s)}$. The displayed identity for $\tau$ makes these transitions compose, and pseudofunctor associativity identifies the two ways of inserting transport compositions. An arrow $a:u\to v$ is sent at level $r$ to $T_{I_{p(r)},\mathfrak m^r}(a_{p(r)})$; its transition square is the transported square for $a$. Transport preserves identities and composites, so this defines a functor $E$ to formal objects on $C$.

source.place: Tag 06H6 (lemma-formal-objects-different-filtration), construction of the functor; Tag 06H3 (definition-formal-objects).

proof.text: Define a functor $G$ in the opposite direction by $(G\xi)_n=T_{\mathfrak m^{q(n)},I_n}\xi_{q(n)}$. If $n'\ge n$, transport the transition of $\xi$ from $q(n')$ to $q(n)$ further to $B_n$ to obtain the transition for $G\xi$. On arrows use transport of the component at $q(n)$. The transition identity and the arrow squares follow by applying the same transport functor to the corresponding identity and square for $\xi$; its functor laws give the functor laws for $G$. Now put $t_n=p(q(n))\ge n$. Composition of transports identifies $(GEu)_n$ with $T_{I_{t_n},I_n}u_{t_n}$, since $I_{t_n}\subseteq\mathfrak m^{q(n)}\subseteq I_n$. The component $\alpha_{u,n}=\tau_{t_n,n}$ is an isomorphism to $u_n$. For $n'\ge n$, both routes in its transition square are the transition $\tau_{t_{n'},n}$: factor it first through $t_n$, respectively first through $n'$. These are equal by the identity in step 2. For an arrow $a:u\to v$, naturality of $\alpha$ is precisely the transition square for $a$ from $t_n$ to $n$. Thus $\alpha:GE\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06H6 (lemma-formal-objects-different-filtration), explicit inverse and first comparison filling the omitted equivalence verification.

proof.text: Put $s_r=q(p(r))\ge r$. Then $(EG\xi)_r$ is canonically $T_{\mathfrak m^{s_r},\mathfrak m^r}\xi_{s_r}$, since $\mathfrak m^{s_r}\subseteq I_{p(r)}\subseteq\mathfrak m^r$. Let $\beta_{\xi,r}$ be the transition of $\xi$ from $s_r$ to $r$. For $r'\ge r$, the two composites in its transition square are the transition from $s_{r'}$ to $r$, factored through $s_r$, respectively through $r'$. The formal-system transition identity equates them. The componentwise arrow square from $s_r$ to $r$ gives naturality in $\xi$. Hence $\beta:EG\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$. The functors $E,G$ with these two natural isomorphisms exhibit an equivalence of groupoids. No descent or lifting property of $\mathcal F$ is used: only its transport functors, their coherent compositions, and the invertible transitions of the given systems occur.

source.place: Tag 06H6 (lemma-formal-objects-different-filtration), second comparison filling the omitted equivalence verification.

proof.text:
Let $\xi=Eu$. Fix $n$ and choose $r\ge q(n)$. Then $\mathfrak m^r\subseteq I_n$ and $p(r)\ge r\ge n$. Evaluate $\xi$ at $B_n$ by transporting its $r$-th component. The composition isomorphism gives
$$T_{\mathfrak m^r,I_n}\xi_r\cong T_{I_{p(r)},I_n}u_{p(r)}\xrightarrow{\tau_{p(r),n}}u_n.$$
Increasing $r$ does not change this comparison: the two maps from any larger component both equal its transition to $u_n$, by the identity for $\tau$. For $n'\ge n$, choose one $r$ at least $q(n')$ and $q(n)$, and increase it until $p(r)\ge n'$. The two comparison paths to $u_n$ are $\tau_{p(r),n}$ and $\tau_{n',n}\circ T_{I_{n'},I_n}(\tau_{p(r),n'})$, which are equal. Arrow naturality is the component square for an arrow of $I$-systems from $p(r)$ to $n$. Thus these evaluation comparisons are compatible in $n$, in the truncation chosen for evaluation, and in $u$.

source.place: Tag 06H6 (lemma-formal-objects-different-filtration), evaluation of its construction; Tag 06H3 (definition-formal-objects).

proof.text: Finally let $a:C\to A$ be a local $R$-map inducing the identity on $k$, factoring as $C\to B_n\xrightarrow{\bar a}A$. With $r\ge q(n)$ as in step 5, $a$ kills $\mathfrak m^r$, so the defining evaluation $\xi_A$ can use $\xi_r$. Transporting the isomorphism in step 5 along $\bar a$ gives $\xi_A\cong\bar a_*u_n$. For a further morphism $A\to A'$ in the test category, the composition isomorphism identifies this comparison transported to $A'$ with the one for the composite map. If a second index also permits the factorization, take a common larger index and a common $r$; the identity for $\tau$ used in step 5 equates both comparisons. These observations also prove compatibility with arrows of systems. For a different formal object isomorphic to $Eu$, compose with that isomorphism and its evaluated components.

lean.statement: theorem formal_filtration_comparison {R k : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Field k] [Algebra R k] [Algebra.FiniteType R k] (F : CofibredGroupoids.{u, v, w} R k) (C : CompleteLocalAlgebra R k) (I : CofinalIdealFiltration C) : ∃ E : FiltrationSystem I F ≌ FormalObject F C, ∃ e : ∀ (s : FiltrationSystem I F) (n : ℕ) (A : TestCategory R k) (f : filtrationTest I n ⟶ A), evaluate (E.functor.obj s) (filtrationLocalMap I n f) ≅ (push F f).obj (s.obj n), (∀ (s t : FiltrationSystem I F) (a : s ⟶ t) (n : ℕ) (A : TestCategory R k) (f : filtrationTest I n ⟶ A), (push F (evaluationMap (filtrationLocalMap I n f))).map ((E.functor.map a).app (nilpotenceIndex A)) ≫ (e t n A f).hom = (e s n A f).hom ≫ (push F f).map (a.app n)) ∧ (∀ (s : FiltrationSystem I F) (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n) (A B : TestCategory R k) (f : filtrationTest I n ⟶ A) (f' : filtrationTest I m ⟶ B) (g : A ⟶ B) (hg : f ≫ g = filtrationMap I h ≫ f'), (push F g).map (e s n A f).hom ≫ (filtrationTransportComparison I s h f f' g hg).hom = (evaluationRestriction (E.functor.obj s) g (filtrationLocalMap I m f') (filtrationLocalMap I n f) (filtrationLocalMap_comp I h f f' g hg)).hom ≫ (e s m B f').hom)
